# Composio App Research & Integration Analysis (100 Apps)
# Machine-readable summary for AI agents and LLMs

## Overview
- Project: Composio AI Product Ops Take-Home Assignment
- Scope: 100 SaaS, DevTool, and Enterprise Applications evaluated for AI agent toolkit buildability.
- Execution: Multi-phase autonomous research pipeline with error-taxonomy verification loops and dual-model + 15-app human spot-check calibration.

## Key Metrics & Recalibrated Reality
- Total Apps: 100 across 10 categories
- Self-Serve Rate: 74.0% (45 Free Tier, 29 Free Trial)
- Gated Rate: 26.0% (11 Paid-Only, 7 Partner/Sales Gated, 5 Admin Approval, 3 No Public API)
- Buildable Today: 78 Yes, 18 Partial, 4 No
- MCP Server Coverage: 14 Official, 27 Community, 59 None (Substantial White-Space Opportunity)
- Empirical Accuracy:
  - In-Sample (N=30): Pass 1 Strict: 80.0% -> Pass 2: 93.3% (+13.3% lift via error taxonomy)
  - Holdout Unseen (N=20): Pass 1 Strict: 75.0% -> Pass 2: 85.0% (+10.0% generalization lift)
  - Provenance: Initial labels by dual-model consensus (Claude & Gemini blind extraction), with 15 critical edge-case cells manually spot-checked by human candidate.

## Actionable Tiers
- Tier 1 (Easy Wins, Build Now): 70 apps (Frictionless self-serve developer access with public REST/GraphQL APIs).
- Tier 2 (Workarounds / Paid / CLI): 17 apps (Requires paid subscription, trial credits, or local CLI wrapper).
- Tier 3 (High-Touch / Partner Gated): 13 apps (Requires enterprise sales outreach, merchant underwriting, or manual developer review).

## Edge Cases & Architectural Traps
- CLI-Only (Not SaaS REST): Sherlock (Python OSINT CLI), Mermaid CLI (npm diagram compiler).
- Ghost APIs (No Public 3rd Party API): fanbasis, Consensus, NotebookLM (consumer app; enterprise via Vertex AI).
- High-Friction Developer Reviews: Google Ads (developer token review), LinkedIn Ads (partner review), Amazon SP-API (AWS SigV4 + seller vetting).

## Tooling Context
- Composio native search retired (HTTP 410); fallback to Tavily and direct HTTP fetchers with disk caching.
- Gemini free-tier rate limits (15 RPM) managed via lightweight fallback extraction models and deterministic caching.
- In-browser simulator is a replay inspector of verified extraction runs.
